fields.location: Task item (c) / skeleton premise: 'given convention 1 (holds for every basis), is C(n,A) now well-defined as a condition on A alone' treated as inert bookkeeping, and its consequence in (b), 'is A tensor B the edge n -> nN_A N_B given by composing the A-edge and B-edge'.
fields.reason: Both sides of C(n,A) are basis-dependent (phi_{nN} must be fed tau_A f_A tau_A^{-1}, not the basis-free f_A). Changing basis by g in GL_N(R) conjugates both sides by G = g^{(+)n}. Hence C(n,A) at all bases is EQUIVALENT to C(n,A) at one basis PLUS the requirement phi_{nN}(G F G^{-1}) = G phi_{nN}(F) G^{-1} for all lifted F and all G in Delta_n(GL_N(R)). Convention 1 therefore does force a (restricted) conjugation-equivariance of Phi, not merely well-definedness; Aut_R-alg(A) is the automatic sub-part of that action and is not superseded. This propagates: C(n,A) & C(nN_A,B) deliver C(n,A tensor B) only at PRODUCT bases, supplying equivariance only under the subgroup generated by GL_{N_A} tensor 1 and 1 tensor GL_{N_B} (dim <= 7 in GL_4 for N_A=N_B=2), while C(n, A tensor B) at every basis demands all of GL_{N_A N_B}(R). So the asserted edge composition is a strict implication in one direction only and the diagram does not commute under convention 1. Secondary gaps: T_A is overloaded (declared A^n -> R^{nN}, applied to phi_n(f) which is not in A^n; the lift-of-output operation and its liftability hypothesis are never introduced); the 'divisibility poset' is a multigraph, not a poset diagram, since non-isomorphic Weil algebras of equal dimension give parallel edges n -> nN; and the (d) overlap is not shown non-degenerate (in standard bases, f_A = g_B with A=R[e]/e^3, B=R[x,y]/(x,y)^2 forces f affine).
fields.audit_scope: Examined at full depth: the type-correctness of the core identity phi_{nN}(f_A)=T_A(phi_n(f)); item (c), the exact logical content of the all-bases quantifier, by explicit change-of-basis computation; item (b), tensor-edge composition, including the product-basis vs all-basis gap and the group generated; item (d), readings of 'vector fields in common' with an explicit n=1, m=3 computation for A=R[e]/e^3 and B=R[x,y]/(x,y)^2 on f(t)=t^2. Examined shallowly: item (a), reduced to (b)+(d) plus a structural note on the poset indexing; the A tensor B =~ B tensor A commuting-square check was identified but not carried out. Not examined: whether Phi is required to be h-parametrized and how h interacts with A (h real vs h in A); order/consistency conditions on Phi; whether any nonzero Phi satisfies the package at all (existence is Balthasar's axis); standing of the result in the literature (Casper's axis). references/ is absent on this branch, so all cited standard facts (Weil algebra definition, T_A o T_B = T_{A tensor B}, low-dimensional classification) are flagged [UNVERIFIED]; the dim-3 witness computation is self-contained and does not rely on the classification.

subtasks.name: (c) content of all-bases quantifier + Aut(A) action
A tensor B =~ B tensor A square commutes

definitional_ambiguity.convention: What '(two lift structures on R^m) have vector fields in common' means in item (d).
readings: (I) Field-level overlap: the same map F : R^m -> R^m lies in both L(n,A) and L(n'',B), i.e. F is simultaneously a basis-presentation of an A-lift and of a B-lift.

(II) Base-field-level overlap: same n, same f : R^n -> R^n, two algebras A, B of equal dimension N; the 'common vector field' is f itself, and phi_m receives one prescription from f_A and one from f_B.
definitional_ambiguity.witness: n=1, N=3, m=3; A = R[e]/(e^3) with basis 1,e,e^2; B = R[x,y]/(x,y)^2 with basis 1,x,y; f(t) = t^2. Then f_A(a0,a1,a2) = (a0^2, 2a0a1, 2a0a2 + a1^2) and f_B(b0,b1,b2) = (b0^2, 2b0b1, 2b0b2), which differ in the third coordinate by a1^2. Under reading (I) this pair is NOT an instance of (d)'s hypothesis at all (f_A =/= f_B; indeed f_A = g_B in standard bases forces f affine). Under reading (II) it IS an instance, and the answer is that the two prescriptions are independent, since they constrain phi_3 at two distinct arguments. The two readings therefore return different answers on this exact case, which round 2's analysis of (d) runs.

petition.subtask: Determine whether the two prescription-domains in (d) intersect at any non-affine vector field once convention 1 is in force, i.e. whether the Delta_n(GL_N(R))-orbit of L(n,A) meets that of L(n'',B) outside the degenerate locus - equivalently, whether a lifted field f_A with f''=/=0 determines its Weil algebra up to isomorphism.
petition.benefit: This is orbit-intersection geometry, qualitatively different from this slot's quantifier and type auditing, and it decides whether the package's stated 'point of interest' has any content: if the overlap is always affine/degenerate, item (d) is vacuous as posed and the whole two-prescriptions motivation collapses, which would relocate the target rather than merely refine it.
